channel.title: The Signal
channel.description: Essays on advanced technology, recent research, the higher-education ecosystem, and student life — written for researchers, engineers, and students.

item.title: Foundation models are quietly rewriting scientific computing
item.description: Large pretrained models are moving from chatbots into simulation, discovery, and lab automation. Here is what changes for the people who actually run the experiments.

item.title: Reproducibility is a feature, not a chore
item.description: Research code that someone else can run a year later is worth more than a clever result nobody can reproduce. A practical checklist for shipping work that survives.

item.title: How to read a machine-learning paper in 20 minutes
item.description: You cannot read every paper front to back, and you should not try. A repeatable method for extracting what matters — fast — without fooling yourself.

item.title: The systems that make a research group healthy
item.description: Great groups are not built on brilliant individuals but on quiet systems — for feedback, credit, and care. What those systems look like, and why they scale trust.

item.title: Doing more with tiny models: edge AI in healthcare
item.description: The most useful medical AI often runs on a wearable, not a data centre. Why small, efficient models matter — and the techniques that make them work.

item.title: From coursework to research: a first-year roadmap
item.description: The jump from taking classes to doing research is the hardest transition in graduate school. A month-by-month way to make it feel less like falling.
